summary: First sftd release published by this repository's pipeline, with SemVer versions shared by the image and the chart. It brings everything since 5.0.60: federated call fixes, Gateway API support and no more Bitnami images. Before upgrading, check image overrides, leftover multiSFT discovery values and, with gateway.enabled, ListenerSet support.

changes.description: The external IP helper image moved from initImage to externalIpHelper.image, the join-call proxy runs nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged as UID 101, and sftd_disco has its own image. If you mirror or override images, set externalIpHelper.image, drop Bitnami nginx overrides of joinCall.image, and mirror quay.io/wire/sftd_disco:1.1.1, docker.io/alpine/kubectl:1.35.1 and docker.io/nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.29.5-alpine3.23-perl.

TURN discovery is gone from the chart. Remove multiSFT.discoveryRequired and multiSFT.turnDiscoveryURL from your values and set multiSFT.turnServerURI or multiSFT.turnServerURIs: with discoveryRequired: true left in, the StatefulSet references a missing volume and is rejected.

With gateway.enabled, HTTPS attaches through a ListenerSet and the GatewayClass defaults to envoy. Install Gateway API CRDs and a controller supporting v1 ListenerSet (tested with Envoy Gateway 1.9.2); an existing Gateway must admit the release namespace in allowedListeners; with a mergeGateways GatewayClass, set gateway.envoyProxy.create: false.

Versioning: releases are SemVer versions instead of 5.0.<build number>. The image quay.io/wire/sftd and the Helm chart share that version, so the chart goes from its 0.x versions to 5.1.0. The chart is still published to the charts-avs Helm repository and also to oci://quay.io/wire/charts/stable/sftd.
An SFT that joins a federated group call already in progress now receives the video streams of the other SFTs.
Federation works with several TURN servers: multiSFT.turnServerURIs spreads the replicas over them.
The chart can run behind Envoy Gateway instead of the nginx Ingress, with TLS 1.3 by default, an optional FIPS 202205 TLS profile and the option to share the wire-ingress Gateway.
mediaIP sets the address sftd advertises to clients; with a host or literal address, the external IP lookup, its node-read RBAC and its startup delay go away.
advertiseInternalIp also advertises the pod address, for an SFT reachable on both an internal and an external address.
clusterDomain supports clusters bootstrapped with a DNS domain other than cluster.local.
The chart lists every image it uses in its helm.sh/images annotation, which helps mirroring.
Pods restart when their secrets change.
When no external IP is found, the pod starts and advertises its host addresses with a warning instead of crash-looping.
The external IP helper and the join-call proxy no longer use Bitnami images and run as non-root, like sftd_disco.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds defaults to 0, so a rollout no longer waits 10 seconds per pod; set it back to 10 to keep the old pause.
sftd logs less when a video SSRC is unknown.

configuration.description: Replaced by externalIpHelper.image; move any override there.
Image of the init container that looks up the node external IP; only used when mediaIP is unset or references __SFT_EXT_IP__.
The join-call proxy moved from Bitnami nginx to nginx-unprivileged; an override must point to a compatible image.
sftd_disco is released separately from sftd and has its own version.
TURN discovery is gone; use multiSFT.turnServerURI or multiSFT.turnServerURIs.
Remove it from your values: set to true, it still renders an init container whose volume no longer exists.
A list of TURN URIs; each replica takes one, round-robin by ordinal. Overrides multiSFT.turnServerURI.
Address advertised for media: __SFT_EXT_IP__ (the default when unset), __SFT_HOST_IP__, __SFT_POD_IP__ or a literal address.
Also advertise the pod address as an ICE candidate; rejected when mediaIP already resolves to the pod address.
Only change it on a cluster bootstrapped with another DNS domain.
Was 10; set it back to keep a pause before a pod stops.
Set to false once the Gateway API path replaces the nginx Ingress.
Gateway API settings (enabled, create, name, namespace, className, listeners, envoyProxy, tls, alpn, proxyProtocol, patchPolicies); gateway.enabled defaults to false. See the chart README.
Applies Envoy's FIPS_202205 TLS profile; needs EnvoyPatchPolicy support and a dedicated, non-merged Gateway.
